Copper-Catalyzed Radical Approach to Allenyl Iodides
 Yulong Song,a Shihua Song,a,b Xinyu Duan,a,b Xiaoyan Wu,a,b Feng Jiang,a,b Yuchen Zhang,a,b Junjie 
Fan,a,b Xin Huang,a,b Chunling Fua and Shengming Ma*a 
 
A copper-catalyzed 1,4-addition reaction of sulfonyl iodides with 
1,3-enynes affording various allenyl halides in high yields under 
mild conditions has been developed. Mechanistic studies showed 
that the reaction proceeds through a radical mechanism.
Recently much attention has been paid to the synthesis1 and 
reactions2 of allenes. Of particular interest, allenyl halides are 
very important building blocks in organic synthesis3-5 as well as 
natural products.6 Common approaches include (1) SN2’-type 
nucleophilic substitution reaction of propargyl mesylates with 
two equivalents each of copper halide and lithium halide 
(Scheme 1 (a));7 (2) electrophilic cyclization of 1,3-enynes 
bearing a nucleophilic unit for the synthesis of trisubstituted 
allenyl halides with a cyclic substituent (Scheme 1 (b)).8 Thus, 
achieving the synthesis of allenyl halides with a high efficiency 
in a catalytic manner is still a challenging work. Here we wish to 
report that a Cu-catalyzed reaction of 1,3-enynes9-12 with aryl 
sulfonyl halides13-14 affording tetrasubstituted allenyl halides 
efficiently. 
We commenced our study by using dodec-1-en-3-yne (1a) and 
TsBr as model substrates. After some trial and error, it was 
observed that propargylic bromide 3a was obtained in 5% yield 
with 65% of 1a being recovered when CuBr (10 mol %) and 1,10-
phen (20 mol %) were employed for the reaction in CHCl3 at 25 
oC after 8 hours. By running the reaction at 50 oC, the yield of 
propargylic bromide 3a was improved to 20% with 43% 
recovery of 1a (Scheme 2, eq. 1). The reaction of 2-
methyldodec-1-en-3-yne (1b) with TsBr at 25 oC also afforded 
propargylic bromide 3b in 13% yield with 57% of 1b being 
recovered. By increasing temperature to 50 oC, the yield of 
propargylic bromide 3b was improved to 41% with 9% recovery 
of 1b (Scheme 2, eq. 2). Interestingly, for the reaction of dodec-

addition to alkyl-substituted (R2) enynes, the reaction of 
different aryl-substituted (R2) enynes with TsI were also studied 
under the standard reaction conditions. It was found that a 
variety of different substitutents including electron-donating

6sa) at the para-, ortho-, or meta-position were well tolerated 
to afford the desired allenyl iodides in good to excellent yields 
(83%-98%). Thienyl-substituted allenyl iodide 6ta and allenyl 
iodide bearing a pyridinyl group 6ta-1 could also be prepared in 
excellent yields. The structures of the products were further 
unambiguously established by X-ray crystallographic analysis of

To gain further insights into the mechanism, some control 
experiments have been carried out (Scheme 4). When the 
reaction was conducted in the presence of  2,2,6,6-tetramethy-
1-piperidinyloxy (TEMPO)16 under standard conditions, it was 
found that no desired product 6ba was detected with 1b being 
recovered in 96% yield. Furthermore, when enyne 7 with a 
cyclopropyl unit at the 2-position was treated with 4a, the ring-
opening enynyl iodide product (E)-8 was produced in 62% yield, 
further indicating a radical mechanism. The configuration of the 
C=C bond in product (E)-8 was determined by nOe study. The 
steric hindrance of Ts may determine the configuration of 
product (E)-8.

On the basis of the experimental results aforementioned, we 
proposed a possible mechanism (Scheme 5). Initially, the LCuI 
species reacts with TsI to afford the LCuI2 species and the p-
methylbenzenesulfonyl free radical via a single electron transfer 
process. Then the p-methylbenzenesulfonyl free radical attacks 
enyne (1) to produce the propargyl radical IN-1, which is in 
resonance with allenyl radical IN-2. These two species IN-1 and 
IN-2 would couple with LCuI2 species to generate propargyl 
copper(III) diiodide species IN-3 and allenyl

Synthetic potential of the products has also been 
demonstrated: (Z)-1,3-enyne 9 can be easily obtained in 100% 
yield by treating 6xa with 1.2 equiv Et3N (Scheme 6). The 
configuration of (Z)-9 was determined by an NOE study. The 
Suzuki coupling reaction of 6pa with aryl or alkenyl boronic

Conclusions
In conclusion, we have developed an efficient method for the 
synthesis of tetrasubstituted allenyl iodides via a copper-
catalyzed 1,4-radical addition reaction of 1,3-enynes. A broad 
range of functional groups were tolerated under mild 
conditions with good to excellent yields. Mechanistic studies 
suggested that the reaction proceeded via a radical pathway 
involving the resonance of propargyl radical with allenyl radical. 
Further studies in this area are being pursued in our laboratory.
